findings.evidence: ReductiveGroups/README.md orders Layer 6 (reductive and semisimple groups) before Layer 7, whose root-datum target is explicitly for `(G,T)` and begins with maximal tori; STATUS.md says Layers 5–8 are untouched and identifies unipotence/reductivity as the next obstacle. The theorem currently applies only to an arbitrary `D(M) → G`, with the module docstring explicitly disclaiming reductivity and maximality.
findings.fix: Defer this new theorem until Layer 6 reductivity and the maximal-torus setup exist on main or in an open prerequisite PR, then connect it directly to that split pair.
findings.issue: This adds Layer 7 root-grading infrastructure while the preceding reductive-group stage and the split maximal torus in a reductive group are absent, making the current specialization speculative.

summary: The bracket theorem is a genuine root-datum prerequisite, but it is being built ahead of the roadmap’s required reductive/maximal-torus stages.
